transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-11-06
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Maya Lopez (Stratus Partnerships); Ethan Park (Stratus Head Infra); Lena Fischer (Stratus SE)

Summary:
Quick partner intro and discovery to understand Stratus' channel and technical capabilities; align on integration patterns (reseller vs managed service), identify technical gating items for Redwood Dedicated/Private deployments, schedule technical benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE on the partnership side; priya's my SE, she'll run the deeper tech follow ups
[00:10] Maya Lopez: hi all, maya here at Stratus, thanks for setting this up — we're looking at potential strategic partners for our managed GPU offering
[00:18] Priya Nair: morning maya, ethan, lena; quick agenda, partner program overview, integration models (reseller vs marketplace vs managed), technical requirements (VPC, KMS, bare-metal), then open q's
[00:30] Ethan Park: yeah from infra we're mostly interested in two things: 1) how tight is the integration for private deployments, and 2) performance / kernel support for H100s and A100s
[00:45] Lena Fischer: and on the SE side we want to know telemetry / observability hooks — like can we send logs to our SIEM, what auditing looks like
[00:55] Alex Chen: absolutely; high level we have three modes — hosted API (fast, simple), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools w/ SLA), and Private (VPC or on-prem for customers). For partners you can resell hosted, run Dedicated on your infra, or integrate Redwood as part of your managed offering
[01:15] Priya Nair: on the tech front, our runtime supports common GPU SKUs, we pick kernels based on model arch and seq length distribution; for H100 we have tested optimized kernels, and we do KV cache + continuous batching to keep token costs down
[01:35] Ethan Park: when you say "tested" are there published perf numbers or benchmarks, or do we run our own? network egress is a concern for us
[01:45] Priya Nair: we have public perf profiles for verified models; for partner/enterprise we usually run a co-benchmark — SE-led, 2-4 hours for a baseline. we can run it on your cluster or ours depending on the integration
[01:58] Maya Lopez: timeline wise, we'd ideally land something in Q1; we need legal + pricing to line up. is there a program fee or margin split typical for partners
[02:10] Alex Chen: typical reseller economics depend on volume; we have partner tiers — for initial pilots often a rev-share or committed capacity model. legal will need to look at reseller terms; we can share a draft
[02:28] Lena Fischer: on security, do you support SSO/SAML, SOC2, and customer-managed KMS/HSM? Also audit logs per token is a hard requirement for some of our customers
[02:40] Priya Nair: yes — SSO/SAML and RBAC are supported; we are SOC 2 type 2 compliant; for Private we integrate with customer KMS (bring-your-own-key) and can provide audit logs. small caveat: some very-low-level audit traces need an on-prem control plane
[03:02] Ethan Park: what about data residency — can instances be pinned to specific regions or on-prem? we operate in eu-west and us-east, and some customers need eu-only
[03:12] Priya Nair: for Private and Dedicated you can pin capacity to regions; hosted has region controls too but if you need eu-only residency for a specific customer, Private or Dedicated is recommended
[03:25] Maya Lopez: integration questions — do you expose a reseller API, or is it more white-label via console? and is billing integrated via API or manual invoicing?
[03:36] Alex Chen: we have APIs for usage, model catalog, and billing; partners can use our console white-labeling options in some tiers. Billing can be automated via API or handled via partner invoicing for reserved contracts
[03:50] Lena Fischer: curious about model catalog — can partners ship their own model bundles or only use Redwood-curated models
[03:58] Priya Nair: partners can bring models; we support onboarding custom model artifacts, version pinning, rollouts, and quantization profiles. we do model vetting for performance and safety
[04:12] Ethan Park: network throughput — what's the typical egress model? we plan to colocate infra and want to know about KV-cache traffic and prefix caching impacts
[04:24] Priya Nair: KV cache is kept on the inference nodes, caching reduces repeated prefix costs; traffic patterns depend on your batching strategy. we can share guidance for autoscale and burst policies to minimize egress
[04:40] Maya Lopez: ok practical ask — can Redwood run a 24-hour benchmark on H100s with our 2 typical workloads? and then a short report with latency percentiles and cost per 1M tokens
[04:53] Alex Chen: yep that's our usual; we'll need workload specs and sample prompts. priya will take the benchmark lead
[05:00] Priya Nair: i'll follow up for the exact runner; usually we do small synthetic + your real prompts for quality checks; we also do a small eval around hallucination/quality regressions
[05:18] Ethan Park: security questionnaire — we'll probably send one (vendor security). how fast is your security pack turnaround, and do you provide contract redlines
[05:28] Alex Chen: we aim to return security packs in 3-5 business days; legal can handle redlines but timelines vary with enterprise counsel; we'll attach SOC2 and our standard security addendum
[05:42] Lena Fischer: any known limits around model size or sequence length on Dedicated vs Private? some customers push towards 70k tokens
[05:52] Priya Nair: sequence length support depends on kernel and memory; we support up to 64k for certain model configs with custom kernels, 70k is possible but we'd need to validate on the specific model and hardware (memory layout matters)
[06:12] Maya Lopez: commercial — we want to understand margin and what a joint go-to-market motion looks like. do you co-sell or is it pure referral
[06:22] Alex Chen: both — we have referral, reseller, and co-sell programs. co-sell is available for larger strategic partners with joint landing pages, joint case studies, and deal registration protections
[06:35] Ethan Park: latency SLOs — what do you guarantee for Dedicated? 95th percentile numbers?
[06:42] Priya Nair: Dedicated SLAs vary by SKU and commitment; typical 95p for generation flows is in the 200-500ms range for small-medium models; large models and long context push that upward. we'll provide per-model profiles
[06:58] Maya Lopez: any blockers on your side for integrating with a partner-managed fleet (we manage k8s and the infra, you provide control plane)?
[07:08] Priya Nair: we do both: self-hosted control plane for Private or hybrid where your ops team runs the infra and we push runtime agents. network egress and KMS are the usual integration points
[07:22] Alex Chen: next steps — we'll send partner materials, priya will schedule the tech deep dive, and maya to share infra diagrams. legal will thread in a draft reseller agreement
[07:34] Maya Lopez: perfect — i'll get the docs over and loop legal
[07:40] Ethan Park: thanks everyone, that was useful
[07:45] Alex Chen: thanks folks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the deck
